questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
MU
In the diagram a consumer’s budget line shifts from GH to JK. J G good Y O K H good X Which statement must be correct?

options.A: The price of good X has increased relative to the price of good Y.
options.B: The prices of both goods have fallen.
options.C: There has been an increase in the consumer’s real income.
options.D: There has been an increase in the consumer’s money income.

questions.questionText: What could cause the demand curve for labour to shift to the left?

options.A: a decrease in immigration
options.B: a decrease in labour productivity
options.C: a fall in real wages
options.D: a rise in the money wage rate

questions.questionText: In the diagram S is an individual worker’s supply of labour curve. S S wage rate O hours of work What could cause the curve to shift from S to S ?

A firm’s workers join a trade union which negotiates an increase in the workers’ wage rate. The increase in the wage rate results in an increase in the number employed by the firm. What could explain this?

options.A: The demand for the firm’s product is price-elastic.
options.B: The firm is a monopsonist within its local labour market.
options.C: The firm operates in a perfectly competitive labour market.
options.D: There is a high degree of substitutability between capital and labour.

questions.questionText: The schedule shows the short-run marginal cost of producing good X. units of X 1 2 3 4 5 marginal cost ($) 40 30 30 60 120 Given that the total fixed cost is $20, what level of output minimises average total cost?

options.A: 2 units B 3 units C 4 units D 5 units

questions.questionText: Which is an example of an external diseconomy?

options.A: difficulties in co-ordinating activities in a large organisation
options.B: difficulties in motivating workers in a large organisation
options.C: higher transport costs as a firm’s market expands
options.D: increased traffic congestion as industries expand

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s demand curve and its marginal revenue curve. P price D O MR quantity What is the approximate price elasticity of demand at price OP?
In the absence of regulation, why is it likely that the market for air travel on the Singapore-Sydney route would be highly contestable?

options.A: An airline entering the market would lose little if it later exited that market.
options.B: The airline industry’s capacity to expand its operations in the short-run is limited.
options.C: The demand for air travel on the Singapore-Sydney route is price-elastic.
options.D: There is no effective substitute for air travel for journeys between Singapore and Sydney.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s marginal and average cost curves. The firm enters a collusive agreement with other firms in the industry. It is agreed that each firm will charge a common price, OP, and will restrict the level of its output to a production quota set by the industry cartel. The firm is allocated a production quota, Oq. MC AC G H P $ K L J M N O q quantity The firm decides to cheat in order to maximise its profits. What is its short-run increase in profits?

options.A: PGKL
options.B: PHJL
options.C: PHJL minus PGNM
options.D: PGKL minus LKNM

questions.questionText: A competitive market becomes a monopoly. What is likely to happen?

options.A: Consumer surplus will be reduced by the amount of the deadweight loss.
options.B: Producer surplus will be reduced by the amount of the deadweight loss.
options.C: The loss in consumer surplus will be balanced by the increase in producer surplus.
options.D: There will be a transfer of surplus from consumer to producer.

questions.questionText: A government requires all its young citizens to undertake community service for a period of 6 months. The wages paid to those on the community service are below what they would otherwise have earned. What effect will this have on recorded GDP and on national welfare? effect on GDP effect on national welfare

options.A: reduction increase
options.B: reduction uncertain
options.C: unchanged increase
options.D: unchanged uncertain

questions.questionText: Between 2008 and 2009 a country’s national income at current prices increased by 15%. At the same time the country experienced 5% inflation. Which index number most closely represents the country’s national income in 2009 at 2008 prices (2008 = 100)?

United States % 2004 2005 2006 Which is the only area to have experienced a contraction in either of its measures of money supply?

options.A: Euro area
options.B: Britain
options.C: Japan
options.D: United States

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between household income and household consumption. C C household consumption O household income What would be likely to cause the household consumption curve to shift from C to C ?
The diagram shows a consumption function for a closed economy with no government. C consumption 45° O Y income What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: At income levels below OY, saving is negative.
options.B: At income levels below OY, there is an inflationary gap.
options.C: The equilibrium level of income is OY.
options.D: The marginal propensity to consume increases as income increases.

questions.questionText: When national income equals $40 000 million and government spending equals $15 000 million, an economy is in equilibrium below full employment. Out of every increase of $100 in national income, $15 is taken in taxes, $30 is spent on imports and $5 is saved. To raise national income to the full employment level of $50 000 million, to which level will the government need to raise its own spending?

options.A: $15 500 million
options.B: $20 000 million
options.C: $25 000 million
options.D: $35 000 million

questions.questionText: In the diagram AS is an economy’s long-run aggregate supply curve. AS AS
The diagram shows the demand curves and supply curves of loanable funds. D
If the money supply is fixed, a decrease in economic activity

options.A: increases interest rates.
options.B: increases the transactions demand for money.
options.C: raises the liquidity preference schedule.
options.D: reduces the income velocity of circulation.

questions.questionText: What could explain why the terms of trade of most developing economies tend to worsen over time?

options.A: Their currencies are over-valued in foreign exchange markets.
options.B: They impose lower barriers on imports than developed economies.
options.C: They produce a narrower range of goods than developed economies.
options.D: They produce goods with a low income elasticity of demand.

questions.questionText: An economy is operating at its natural rate of unemployment. According to monetarist theory, what will be the effect on unemployment in the short run and in the long run of an unanticipated increase in the money supply? short run long run

options.A: no change no change
options.B: no change reduction
options.C: reduction no change
options.D: reduction reduction

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between the rate of increase in wages and the rate of unemployment. rate of increase in wages O rate of unemployment What would be likely to cause the curve in the diagram to shift downwards and to the left?

options.A: a reduction in regional differences in unemployment rates
options.B: an increase in the proportion of the workforce belonging to trade unions
options.C: an increase in the unemployment rate
options.D: the expectation of a higher rate of inflation

questions.questionText: Which policy is most likely to reduce a balance of payments deficit without causing inflation?

options.A: a devaluation of the exchange rate
options.B: an increase in import tariffs
options.C: an increase in indirect taxes
options.D: an increase in direct taxes

questions.questionText: Which is most likely to result in an increase in the natural rate of unemployment?

options.A: a decrease in government expenditure on goods and services
options.B: a decrease in the level of government payments to the unemployed
options.C: an increase in trade union membership
options.D: an increase in interest rates

questions.questionText: An economy has underemployed resources. Which method of financing an increase in government expenditure is likely to have the greatest expansionary effect?

options.A: borrowing from the central bank
options.B: borrowing from the non-bank private sector
options.C: increased direct taxation
options.D: increased indirect taxation

questions.questionText: What will be the impact of an increase in marginal tax rates?

options.A: an increase in the propensity to save
options.B: an increase in the value of the investment multiplier
options.C: a strengthening of work incentives
options.D: a strengthening in the operation of automatic stabilisers

questions.questionText: Which is a correct statement about efficiency?

options.A: Allocative efficiency occurs when marginal revenue equals marginal cost.
options.B: An economy is productively efficient when it is producing at a point on its production possibility curve.
options.C: An economy will improve its allocative efficiency when its production possibility curve moves outward.
